forecasts.label: Capital expenditure

news_drafts.headline: Hertfordshire Cabinet asked to approve £7.107m for four SEND units, adding up to 88 places
news_drafts.lead:
Hertfordshire County Council's Cabinet is asked on 4 November 2026 to approve £7.107m of capital spending on four special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) units in mainstream schools. The units would provide up to 88 places for children with cognition and learning needs, across two maintained schools and two academies.

The money comes from a SEND capital budget of £147.343m. Cabinet approved a budget of £140m in February 2026 and on 16 September 2026 agreed to allocate a further £7.343m. The paper says the budget is funded from existing grant allocations, S106 agreements (payments from developers) and borrowing within the approved funding envelope. £40.130m is already approved or under consideration, so this request would take the total committed to £47.237m. The paper says the remaining budget would then fall to £100.106m.

A fifth proposal, a specialist resource provision at St Peter's C of E (VA) Primary School in Rickmansworth, "is not being progressed at this stage". Feasibility work found operational, accommodation and organisational issues. The paper says the school remains committed and that more time will be allowed to refine the proposal and delivery arrangements.

news_drafts.headline: Hertfordshire pension fund rebalances £3bn portfolio to meet new legal deadline
news_drafts.lead: Hertfordshire's Local Government Pension Scheme has established new investment allocations across nine asset classes to comply with regulations introduced by the Pension Schemes Act 2026. The revised Investment Strategy Statement must be published by 31 March 2027, with the Pensions Committee to approve a draft on 23 October and final approval targeted for February 2027. The fund has set strategic ranges for listed equities at 34.5 per cent, credit at 16.5 per cent, and UK government bonds at 13.5 per cent, with defined rebalancing ranges to maintain risk controls while minimising transaction costs. Officers are also recommending a flexible local investment allocation of 0 to 5 per cent, working with the Border to Coast investment pool, which expects to deploy funds from December 2026. However, Hertfordshire's pending Local Government Reorganisation has made it impossible to resolve key implementation questions about return targets, local investment priorities and impact measurement, deferring those decisions pending clarity on the council's future structure.

findings.headline: The Shenley Primary risk register records visible damp in the building and a roof above the proposed unit that has not been replaced.
findings.detail: The register rates the roof and damp risk as Medium likelihood and High impact. A structural survey is underway as part of feasibility, and any remedial costs will be added to the cost plan.
findings.matters: A condition risk identified before construction, with High impact, is the kind of cost exposure that can move a capital estimate.
findings.quote: Visible damp is present within the building, indicating potential water ingress or inadequate ventilation

findings.headline: The paper says the costs of the four schemes remain subject to further feasibility design and surveys, and that a central contingency is held for the academy scheme.
findings.detail: The £7.107m estimate includes allowances for contingencies and is based on reasonable assumptions for risks identified early. The paper does not state the amount of the central contingency.
findings.matters: A finance officer approving a capital figure before surveys are complete will want to know how much is held centrally and that the paper does not give that amount.
findings.figures: £7.107m high-level cost estimate; contingency amount not stated
findings.quote: The final costs remain, subject to further feasibility design and surveys work.

findings.headline: At Hitchin Boys’ School, the temporary use of the Bancroft building will delay realising a capital receipt of circa £750k by 24-36 months.
findings.detail: The Youth Centre space at the front of the Bancroft building has been identified for disposal. The school's temporary use of the adjacent accommodation for its Sixth Form is the cause of the delay.
findings.matters: A council relying on asset disposals to fund capital can see that a receipt has been pushed back by two to three years to enable a SEND scheme.
findings.quote: the temporary use of the adjacent accommodation by Hitchin Boys’ Sixth Form students will mean a delay of around 24-36 months for realising this capital receipt with a value of circa £750k.

findings.headline: The proposed SEND unit at St Peter’s C of E (VA) Primary School, Rickmansworth, is not being progressed at this stage.
findings.detail: Feasibility work found operational, accommodation and organisational issues. The paper says the school remains committed, and that more time will be allowed to refine the proposal and delivery arrangements.
findings.matters: A scheme that was in the programme has been dropped from this tranche after feasibility, which a peer council planning a similar SRP would want to know about.
findings.quote: the proposed Specialist Resource Provision (SRP) at St Peter's C of E (VA) Primary School, Rickmansworth, is not being progressed at this stage.

findings.headline: The paper puts the average cost of an independent placement at £40k more than a place in a SEND unit, and says initial revenue costs will rise before savings arrive.
findings.detail: Funding per place follows the banding model within the High Needs Block. The paper says the units should reduce independent placements, transport costs and pressure on special schools, but it does not quantify the revenue cost or the expected saving.
findings.matters: A finance director weighing a capital spend against higher-cost placements needs to know whether the saving is quantified, and this paper gives the per-place gap but no total.
findings.figures: £40k average cost difference per placement; 88 additional places
findings.quote: The average cost of an independent placement is £40k greater than the cost of a place in a unit.
